newsitem.title: UK: UK physical grain markets see active trading.
newsitem.headline: UK physical grain markets see active trading.

text.p: Early trading on the UK physical markets was active on Wednesday triggered by lower futures and fob prices.
Traders said fob prices started to drift off later on Tuesday and during this morning and this coupled with lower futures on the back of strong sterling brought sellers into the market.
But trade fizzled out as the futures rose on short covering.
"Futures started lower but are now almost back to unchanged mainly on short covering, also many people on the physical side are long and pulled out when prices kept dropping," said a trader.
Delivered business was going on at around one stg below Tuesday's levels with feed wheat fetching 99.25 and 99 stg for Apr/Jun in East Anglia.
On the south coast 94.50 stg was paid for Jan and 96 stg for Feb.
Feed barley was trading at 97 stg for spot material in East Anglia with 98.50 and 98 stg paid in Southampton.
Feed wheat traded at 96 stg a tonne for 2,400 tonnes fob ex-east coast ports while 98 stg was paid for Apr/Jun.
